item.title: Former Pakistan cricketers slam PCB chief Mohsin Naqvi over T20 World Cup 2026 withdrawal threat
item.description: Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman Mohsin Naqvi held a meeting with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad on Monday (January 26) to discuss the government's stand on T20 World Cup 2026 participation after Bangladesh’s removal from the tournament. Following the meeting, Naqvi confirmed through social media that a final call is expected on either Friday (January 30) or Monday (February 2). item.title: “Put in easy group to qualify for next round,” Sunil Gavaskar’s blunt verdict on India vs Pakistan T20 World Cup clash
item.description: With only 10 days remaining for the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup 2026, India batting legend Sunil Gavaskar has criticized the team groupings for the showpiece tournament. Not the one to mince his words, Gavaskar highlighted that India and Pakistan feature in an easy Group A along with Namibia, USA, and Netherlands, ensuring easier qualification to the next round. item.title: “They keep moving from one format to other,” Rahul Dravid weighs in on Team India’s dipping Test performance
item.description: While India’s white-ball side has been performing exceptionally well under head coach Gautam Gambhir, producing trophies and strong win-loss records, that success has not translated to the traditional format. With Gambhir at the helm, India have won seven, lost 10 and drew two of their 19 Tests so far, which includes a couple of clean sweeps against New Zealand (0-3) and South Africa (0-2) at home. item.title: Washington Sundar resumes batting practice at CoE; India to remain patient with all-rounder ahead of T20 World Cup: Report
item.description: India all-rounder Washington Sundar has resumed batting practice as part of his rehabilitation at the BCCI Center of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru, TOI reported on Wednesday (January 28). According to the report, the session lasted for about 30 minutes. While it was a positive step forward in Sundar’s recovery process, discomfort around his rib area continues to persist. item.description: Pakistan skipper Salman Ali Agha was left irked when asked about Babar Azam’s form during a press conference ahead of the T20I series against Australia. item.title: “I can’t do anything…”: Sarfaraz Khan reflects on repeated India snub; feels lucky to be picked by CSK
item.description: Mumbai batter Sarfaraz Khan may have fallen out of favour with the national selectors, but he continues to grind in domestic cricket. Sarfaraz, who has 5,090 first-class runs to his name at an average of 65.25 in 61 matches, has represented India in six Tests so far, scoring 371 runs with the help of one hundred and three half-centuries. item.title: USA batter Aaron Jones provisionally suspended over alleged match fixing
item.description: The International Cricket Council (ICC) on Wednesday (January 28) provisionally suspended USA batter Aaron Jones over alleged fixing during the BIM10 league in Barbados back in the 2023-2024 season. item.title: IND v NZ 2026: “We wanted to see if…,” Suryakumar Yadav explains India’s decision to play 6 batters in 4th T20I
item.description: Team India went with the combination of six batters and five specialist bowlers in the penultimate T20I against New Zealand in Visakhapatnam on Wednesday (January 28). However, the move backfired as the Kiwis racked up a formidable 215/7 on the board and then bundle out the Men in Blue for just 165 in 18.4 overs to secure a thumping 50-run victory. item.title: “Defending champions start as clear favourites,” Ravi Shastri backs India to win back-to-back T20 World Cup titles
item.description: Team India look to be in belligerent form ahead of the T20 World Cup 2026 and will enter the tournament as a formidable contender to retain their title. In the lead up to the marquee event, the Suryakumar Yadav-led side is currently hosting New Zealand in a five-T20I series. The Men in Blue have already gained an unassailable lead in the series after winning first three matches. item.title: IND v NZ 2026: “I can’t be the same as I was,” Shivam Dube reflects on his 'upgrade' journey after 15-ball fifty in 4th T20I
item.description: India may have lost the fourth T20I by 50 runs against New Zealand in Visakhapatnam on Wednesday (January 28), but Shivam Dube left a lasting impression on everyone with his explosive batting.
